title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-harper-nguyen
body:
Sales / Partnership scratch notes — Harper Nguyen

Context:
- Early outreach to TaskFlow AI (YC '22) — workflow automation + LLM layer. Good fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private (data privacy + predictable latency for customer-facing automations).
- Goal: intro + explore joint GTM (embed Redwood inference as recommended runtime for customers using TaskFlow orchestration).

Account snapshot (quick):
- Company: TaskFlow AI
- HQ: SF
- ARR (est): $8-12M (mid-market focus)
- Team size: ~45 (product + eng heavy)
- Public mentions: recently announced "TaskFlow orchestration SDK v2" (May 2024) w/ plugin system for runtimes
- Tech signals: uses Kubernetes + AWS, experiments with Triton for inference; currently recommending hosted LLM providers in docs (no bundled inference).

Key stakeholders (from LinkedIn + GitHub):
- Priya Shah — Head of Partnerships (main outreach target)
- Miguel Alvarez — Head of Product, previously at ScaleAI (technical buyer)
- Dana Lee — Lead Backend Engineer (involved in infra/Runtimes decisions)
- Potential champion: Developer Evangelist (handles integrations and sample apps)

Primary use cases we can lead with:
- Low-latency customer-facing automations (chat + action triggers) where predictable tail latency matters
- Private deployment offering for enterprise customers worried about data residency + auditability
- Cost-optimized dedicated pools for high-throughput automation pipelines (batching + KV cache fitting nicely)

Why Redwood (value props to emphasize):
- Predictable latency SLOs and reserved capacity (Dedicated) for customer-facing automations
- Private deployment + KMS/HSM for compliance-sensitive enterprise customers
- Smart routing + fallback: can route to cheaper model variants for non-critical paths — reduce unit economics for TaskFlow customers
- Developer experience: same API across hosted/dedicated/private so TaskFlow can recommend one integration surface to customers

Potential objections and quick reframes:
- "We already recommend hosted LLMs — why add Redwood?"
  - Response: Redwood reduces operational burden while giving TaskFlow customers an on-ramp to predictable latency + cheaper dedicated options as they scale; integration surface is one API across modes (less customer support burden).
- "Integration complexity / maintenance cost"
  - Response: We provide example plugins, starter repo, and SDKs; can co-build a Quickstart in 2-3 days with our SolutionsEng. Offer a short pilot (30-60d) with a dev environment and sample SLA.
- "Pricing concerns — customers on hosted providers to cut cost"
  - Response: Show TCO model: for sustained traffic, Dedicated pools + batching yields 30-60% lower per-token cost vs pay-as-you-go hosted. Offer a joint TCO review for 3 customer archetypes.
- "Security / data residency"
  - Response: Private deployment plus KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; can run in customer VPC or on-prem.

Outbound drafts (short, pick one):
1) Short intro (cold):
Subject: TaskFlow + Redwood — runtime option for predictable automations
Hi Priya — I run partnerships at Redwood Inference. Saw TaskFlow’s new plugin SDK — congrats. We help companies offer a single inference runtime that customers can consume across hosted, dedicated, or private deployments (predictable latency + lower TCO for sustained traffic). Would love 20m to explore if a co-branded quickstart for your integrators makes sense.

2) Technical touch (after interest):
Subject: Pilot idea — dedicated inference pool for TaskFlow customer pilot
Priya / Miguel — quick follow up: we can spin up a dedicated pool + sample TaskFlow plugin for a 30d pilot (no commitment). Plan: 1) sample plugin + quickstart, 2) pilot on 1-2 customer flows, 3) shared TCO + performance report. Can you share 2-3 candidate flows?

3) DM draft (LinkedIn):
Priya — congrats on v2 launch! I’m Harper at Redwood Inference — we help platform teams add a predictable runtime option for LLMs (low tail latency + private deployments). Quick question — would you be open to a 10-15m intro next week?

Notes on cadence / follow-up:
- Wait 4-5 business days after email, then send technical touch with pilot offer.
- If no response after 2 touches, try mutual connection (Evangelist).

Objection handling snippets (cheat sheet):
- "We don’t own inference": "We can be the recommended runtime partner for your customers — you don’t need to operate it; customers can pick modes that fit them."
- "ROI unclear": offer a short TCO template + sample numbers (we have benchmarks for encoder-decoder and decoder-only workloads).
- "Security concerns": reference Private deployment + audit logs + KMS + customer references (anonymized).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Draft intro email variation with Samir (done: v1)
- [ ] Create 1-page pilot outline (owner: Samir) — include sample metrics to track (latency p50/p95, per-token cost, availability)
- [ ] PR for TaskFlow plugin starter repo (owner: Lena) — aim for 2-week turnaround
- [ ] Schedule intro with Priya — target week of Oct 7
- [ ] Add TaskFlow to partner playbook (Confluence) if pilot goes ahead

Quick numbers to reference in pilot one-pager (examples):
- Baseline hosted (pay-as-you-go) cost estimate: $0.08 / 1k tokens (example)
- Dedicated pool amortized: $0.03-0.05 / 1k tokens at scale (depends on shape + batching)
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for small chat payloads on Dedicated for 8k context models (example)

Random notes / snippets to keep: (raw)
- Potential co-marketing: webinar + case study after pilot
- Could bundle a free 30d trial for 3 mutual customers to seed references
- Look up who ran infra at ScaleAI (Miguel background) — he cares about latency guarantees

-- end scratchpad --

(Internal: Harper — save a clean copy to Confluence once pilot outline is stable; keep this doc as working notes and cadence tracker.)
